slides.title: Hybi's 30-second neutral finder
slides.sub: Try it lying on a mat!

sections.heading: 1. Pelvic see-saw
lines: ① Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
② Gently flatten your lower back, then arch it.
③ Settle about halfway, a small gap underneath.
④ Breathe easy and repeat 5 times.

sections.heading: 2. Get advice if…
lines: or your leg tingles — stop and get it checked.

slides.heading: Get assessed if you notice

caption:
"Find your neutral spine." Momo heard the cue and froze, breath held, tummy clenched.

Neutral simply means your spine's natural curves are there, not flattened or exaggerated. It's a comfortable zone rather than one exact spot, and it looks a little different on everyone. In Pilates it's a reference point for control, not a rule that your back should never bend. Healthy spines round, arch and twist all day, and many exercises move out of neutral on purpose.

Try the pelvic see-saw lying down, settle about halfway, and keep effort light and breathing easy. Our clinical Pilates team at Hybrid Physio starts with an assessment. Book online via the link in bio.
